contracts.commit_point: The user_id filter and result construction in list_user_orders (agent/core/order/repository.py lines 27-45) and the joint match test plus uniform None return in get_order_detail (repository.py lines 48-62).
contracts.declared_mechanism: Joint identity scoping in the order repository: list_user_orders filters order['user_id'] == user_id before building results; get_order_detail requires both user_id and the normalized order_id to match and returns None uniformly for unauthorized and nonexistent orders.
contracts.forbidden_condition: Returning order data on the basis of order_id alone (cross-user order read, including under model prompt injection per repository.py lines 1-5), or emitting responses that let a caller distinguish 'order does not exist' from 'order belongs to another user' (order enumeration).
pending_binding_information: Whether core.logistics.get_shipment_timeline applies equivalent user_id + order_id joint scoping (source not supplied).
Whether core.ticket operations provide equivalent joint scoping and anti-enumeration behavior (source not supplied).
contracts.protected_operation: Order list and detail reads served to the user-private order tools: list_user_orders and get_order_detail.
contracts.protected_resource: Order records in the local order snapshot data/digital_orders. backing query_user_orders and query_order_detail.
contracts.protection_obligation: Order reads must be scoped to the trusted user: list_user_orders and get_order_detail may return order records only when the stored order user_id equals the caller's user_id (joint user_id + order_id filtering), and unauthorized lookups must be indistinguishable from nonexistent ones (uniform empty result).
scope_limits: Covers only the order snapshot repository; shipment reads (core.logistics) and ticket operations (core.ticket) are separate modules whose sources are not supplied.
Defense-in-depth layer behind the interceptor: it assumes the user_id argument it receives, which the interceptor forces to the trusted value; the repository does not itself authenticate identity.

The snapshot is a demo read-only data file ('Replaced by the order center API after the real mall is connected', repository.py line 22); no filesystem mutation is guarded, so no separate file-stratum commit point is asserted.

contracts.commit_point: The middleware decision ahead of call_next(request) at app_main.py lines 36-41: failing requests receive the 403 response and never proceed to route handlers.
contracts.declared_mechanism: FastAPI HTTP middleware same_origin_api registered via @app.middleware("http") in app/app_main.py, returning a 403 JSONResponse for failing requests before call_next.
contracts.forbidden_condition: A cross-site or marker-less write: request path starts with '/api/', method not in {GET, HEAD, OPTIONS}, and either x-requested-with != 'SupportAgent' or (Origin present and urlsplit(origin).netloc != Host header).
pending_binding_information: Whether /api/chat, /api/workspace, or /api/auth handlers dispatch agent tools or lifecycle hooks (app/router/chat.py, app/router/workspace.py, app/router/auth.py and app/service/chat_service.py not supplied).
Whether any agent-mediated effect commits downstream of these /api writes, which would bind this middleware to agent mediation.
contracts.protected_operation: State-changing HTTP writes to the /api/* route surface (chat, workspace, and auth routers mounted under the /api prefix).
contracts.protected_resource: The /api/* endpoints of the FastAPI application (chat.router, workspace.router, auth.router).
contracts.protection_obligation: State-changing requests to /api/* must be same-origin and carry a non-simple request marker: non-GET/HEAD/OPTIONS writes without x-requested-with: SupportAgent, or with an Origin header whose netloc does not match the Host header, must be rejected with 403 before reaching route handlers.
scope_limits: Applies only to paths starting with '/api/' and methods outside {GET, HEAD, OPTIONS}; safe methods bypass the check entirely.
Requests without an Origin header pass if the x-requested-with marker matches; the check relies on the deployment preserving the browser Host header (comment at app_main.py lines 34-35).

No supplied source binds these /api writes to an agent tool, agent lifecycle hook, or agent-generated input reaching a guarded effect; per study scope rules this obligation is recorded without an agent-mediation claim until such a dataflow is shown.

contracts.commit_point: Inside inject_user_id at each MCP tool-call dispatch, immediately before handler(request): PermissionError raised at user_context.py lines 41-43 on missing identity; the sanitized request is committed via handler(request.override(args=new_args)) at user_context.py lines 45-47.
contracts.declared_mechanism: inject_user_id async MCP tool interceptor (agent/core/security/user_context.py) registered as tool_interceptors=[inject_user_id] on each MultiServerMCPClient in BillingAgentNode and AfterSalesAgentNode; it rewrites request.args so user_id equals request.runtime.context.user_id before invoking the handler, and raises PermissionError when the trusted identity is missing.
contracts.forbidden_condition: A user-private MCP tool call reaching the MCP handler with a user_id argument originating from the model rather than the trusted runtime context, or any dispatch of a protected tool when the runtime context carries no truthy user_id (PermissionError refusal path).

contracts.protected_operation: MCP tool-call dispatch of query_user_orders, query_order_detail, query_shipment_timeline, create_after_sales_ticket, query_user_tickets, query_ticket_detail, and escalate_ticket_to_human.
contracts.protected_resource: The current login user's private order, shipment-timeline, and after-sales ticket records exposed through the Digital Commerce MCP server.
contracts.protection_obligation: Every dispatch of a user-private MCP tool (query_user_orders, query_order_detail, query_shipment_timeline, create_after_sales_ticket, query_user_tickets, query_ticket_detail, escalate_ticket_to_human) must execute only with the trusted UserContext identity: the inject_user_id interceptor overrides any model-supplied user_id with the runtime-context identity and refuses the call with PermissionError when no trusted identity exists.
scope_limits: Only the seven tool names in protected_tools are guarded; public catalog/knowledge tools pass through unmodified (user_context.py lines 36-37).

Guarding is per-client: only agent nodes that construct MultiServerMCPClient with tool_interceptors=[inject_user_id] are covered; supplied source shows registrations only in BillingAgentNode and AfterSalesAgentNode.

Agents build UserContext from state.get('user_id', 'unknown') (billing_agent.py line 34; after_sales_agent.py line 41); supplied source does not show upstream authentication of state['user_id'], and a literal 'unknown' default would satisfy the interceptor's truthiness check instead of triggering the PermissionError path.
In-process tools appended outside the MCP client (e.g., search_after_sales_policies and search_technical_documents at after_sales_agent.py line 101) are not intercepted.
Interceptor behavior depends on langchain_mcp_adapters MCPToolCallRequest.runtime/override semantics, whose implementation is not in supplied source.
